top_story: A deadly Houthi strike on Riyadh’s airport on 11 October, followed by another hit on King Khalid airport, punctured Saudi Arabia’s cultivated image of domestic security and exposed how the Yemen war can still reach the kingdom’s social and economic core. The same conflict is also exacting a mass civilian toll at sea: a boat carrying 305 people toward Yemen capsized off Djibouti that day, killing at least 139 migrants, including children, and underscoring how instability continues to pull vulnerable people into lethal routes. In Gaza, Israeli soldiers’ accounts published on 12-13 October describe a recent targeting shift that treated even low-level militants as worth civilian casualties and, in some cases, involved killing unarmed men later labeled terrorists. Taken together, these developments show regional wars bleeding across borders and institutions alike, deepening public insecurity while eroding the moral and political restraints that protect civilians.
